summary: The root مَحَقَ (maḥaqa) means to diminish, deprive of blessing, or completely obliterate something, leaving no trace. It implies a total doing away with.
lane: 1 مَحَقَ ذ , aor. مَحَقَ , inf. n. مَحْقٌ , He rendered a thing deficient, and deprived it of its blessing, or increase: or [ he annihilated, annulled, or obliterated, it;] he did away with it wholly, so that no trace thereof remained. (Msb.) -b2- أَعْمَدُ مِنْ كَيْلٍ , or مُحِقَ : see عَمَدَ .

headwords.def: مَحَقَ, aor. مَحَقَ, inf. n. مَحْقٌ, He rendered a thing deficient, and deprived it of its blessing, or increase: or [ he annihilated, annulled, or obliterated, it;] he did away with it wholly, so that no trace thereof remained. (Msb.) أَعْمَدُ مِنْ كَيْلٍ, or مُحِقَ: see عَمَدَ.
لَيَالِى المُحَاقِ: see دَأْدَآءٌ and الدَّعْجَآءُ.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
